identification.source_of_variation: Abolishment of the Multi-fibre Arrangement (MFA) quotas on Chinese textile and clothing goods following China's accession to the WTO (Phases I-III removed January 2002, Phase IV January 2005); across-firm variation comes from whether a Danish T&C firm produced MFA quota goods in 1999, before the accession.

key_assumptions.assumption: Parallel trends: absent the MFA quota abolishment, firms that produced MFA quota goods in 1999 and other Danish textile and apparel manufacturers would have followed the same trend in the outcome, conditional on firm and year fixed effects.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Aggregate trends in the industry are controlled for with year fixed effects and firm fixed effects absorb level differences; Table A-7 in the online Appendix reports year-by-year employment changes since 1995 for 1995 MFA producers and the paper states these confirm there was no significant impact until 2002.

key_assumptions.assumption: No anticipation: firms did not adjust before 2002 in expectation of the quota removal, because there was a great deal of uncertainty about China's WTO membership and its timing during the 1990s.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper documents recurring uncertainty about China's accession in contemporaneous press reports and states that the empirical strategy utilizes the uncertainty associated with the WTO accession of China; the Phase I and II removals of 1995 and 1998, from which China did not benefit, are used as a validation.

key_assumptions.assumption: No interference: the quota removal does not spill over from MFA quota goods producers onto the comparison group of other textile, clothing and non-T&C firms.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper states outright that this empirical approach does not address potential spillovers from MFA producers on other T&C and non-T&C firms; no evidence is offered that they are absent.

key_assumptions.assumption: Conditional on firm and year fixed effects, exposure to the quota removal is unrelated to other determinants of the outcome; the shock to the competitive environment is exogenous because it was driven by China's WTO accession rather than by Danish demand or supply.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper states the strategy exploits the exogenous trade shock due to China's accession to the WTO and that firm fixed effects can be correlated with the regressors and thus further help to reduce the endogeneity concerns.

key_assumptions.assumption: Treatment status is conditioned on the 1999 product portfolio, before China's WTO accession, so that endogenous product dropping after 2002 does not select the treatment group.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper states that to prevent biased results from such selection within the treatment group, the treatment group is set as those firms that in 1999 produced goods subject to MFA quotas; it notes the results are robust to using 1995 or 1998 instead.

key_assumptions.assumption: 1999 MFA-quota-good import status is not itself an endogenous response to the coming competition, so the triple-difference term isolates the import/offshoring channel rather than a differential propensity to adjust.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper motivates the triple difference by noting that producer-importers' presence in the treatment group would be expected to mute the negative effect, and measures import status in 1999; no test of the exogeneity of import status is reported.

claims.statement: Intensified Chinese low-wage competition from the MFA quota abolishment, measured by MFAQ2RevShare99_i x Dum02_t raises log number of new non-T&C products for Danish textile and apparel manufacturers, scaled by their 1999 MFA quota-good exposure share (Table 7, Panel C., col (6)).

definition.value: Difference-in-differences interaction of the share of firm i's 1999 sales generated from 2002-quota goods (MFAQ2) with Dum02_t, the dummy equal to 1 on and after 2002.

timing.value: exposure share measured in 1999; treatment switched on from 2002 onwards

population.description: Danish textile and apparel manufacturers, 1996-2004 (928 firms for intangibles, 699-716 firms for product churning).
subgroups_defined: firms producing 2002-quota goods in 1999 versus other T&C manufacturers
population.selection: Firm accounting data and the domestic production dataset; the sample period is 1996-2004 because new products are not defined in 1995 and dropped products are not defined in 2005

identification.source_of_variation: Abolishment of the Multi-fibre Arrangement (MFA) quotas on Chinese textile and clothing goods following China's accession to the WTO (Phases I-III removed January 2002, Phase IV January 2005); across-firm variation comes from whether a Danish T&C firm produced MFA quota goods in 1999, before the accession.

key_assumptions.assumption: Parallel trends: absent the MFA quota abolishment, firms that produced MFA quota goods in 1999 and other Danish textile and apparel manufacturers would have followed the same trend in the outcome, conditional on firm and year fixed effects.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Aggregate trends in the industry are controlled for with year fixed effects and firm fixed effects absorb level differences; Table A-7 in the online Appendix reports year-by-year employment changes since 1995 for 1995 MFA producers and the paper states these confirm there was no significant impact until 2002.

key_assumptions.assumption: No anticipation: firms did not adjust before 2002 in expectation of the quota removal, because there was a great deal of uncertainty about China's WTO membership and its timing during the 1990s.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper documents recurring uncertainty about China's accession in contemporaneous press reports and states that the empirical strategy utilizes the uncertainty associated with the WTO accession of China; the Phase I and II removals of 1995 and 1998, from which China did not benefit, are used as a validation.

key_assumptions.assumption: No interference: the quota removal does not spill over from MFA quota goods producers onto the comparison group of other textile, clothing and non-T&C firms.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper states outright that this empirical approach does not address potential spillovers from MFA producers on other T&C and non-T&C firms; no evidence is offered that they are absent.

key_assumptions.assumption: Conditional on firm and year fixed effects, exposure to the quota removal is unrelated to other determinants of the outcome; the shock to the competitive environment is exogenous because it was driven by China's WTO accession rather than by Danish demand or supply.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper states the strategy exploits the exogenous trade shock due to China's accession to the WTO and that firm fixed effects can be correlated with the regressors and thus further help to reduce the endogeneity concerns.

key_assumptions.assumption: Treatment status is conditioned on the 1999 product portfolio, before China's WTO accession, so that endogenous product dropping after 2002 does not select the treatment group.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper states that to prevent biased results from such selection within the treatment group, the treatment group is set as those firms that in 1999 produced goods subject to MFA quotas; it notes the results are robust to using 1995 or 1998 instead.
